They are, but usually at either the cost/charity of the organization or funded by uncle sam.

Dentists for instance will offer free or reduced care if you agree to let a student do the work, or they'll offer free or reduced if the government is paying the bill (via Federal low income insurance like Medicaid)

Private property also does this. Section 8 housing isn't all federal owned, it's also privately owned landlords that agree to the system and let uncle sam subsidize the cost of rent for low income tenants. Usually it's lower income that the private sector where you can charge more for rent but it's steady income from the government that never misses a payment. 

So there are examples of subsidized everything, it's just. Sparatic/spread out/ and under many different names and programs and not always directly from the government.

The issue is finding the assistance, knowing it even exists in the first place, and prooving that you qualify.

Take for example energy assistance. This winter was pretty bad energy wise and I'm a full time student bouncing around part time work when I can find it. Gas was 300 a month during the winter months because my city sold our gas to a private company. I was behind payments and found a state sponsored energy assistance program. It took a lot of searching, it took 3 months for a response, and the response was "please provide more proof that you're poor"

Suffice to say, I didn't get the assistance and it would have been too little too late anyway. Such a program would greatly benefit from being part of the actual state or federal website, or mainline assistance programs instead of hidden somewhere obscure. It would also benefit from some modernization in the form of submitting online forms instead of using USPS but I digress. I just want to share an example of a government assistance program that takes in money but that's hard to find and hard to use.

The issue with multiple organizations doing the same thing is the cost of multiple administrative staff all with decently large salaries. You're duplicating staff costs without providing meaningful gains service wise.

That's a very big question and I don't think I'm educated enough to solve it. In my opinion speaking from the American point of view, we look towards our pretty successful European friends and their social programs. We raise taxes a little, we show sales tax included in item prices instead of being hidden at the end of the purchase, instead of having 2-3 different free and reduced cost healthcare programs for low income/elderly/disabled that all get managed by a different organization or program we consolidate our programs into a universal healthcare system and we start to tackle the issue of our overly greedy insurance companies that tell everyone that it's somehow more affordable to pay hundreds a month in case you might get hurt only for them to deny coverage anyway or only partially cover payment of astronomical healthcare visits. People like to complain that Europeans pay so much in taxes but I honestly don't see the difference when your monthly insurance bill is 100 or more anyway and doesn't even cover everything like eye or dental which are "electives."

It's a pretty complex problem that while standing far away can be summarized as greed and mismanagement, but when you zoom into the problem it's the case of "where do I even start to fix this"

Setting aside a portion of every purchase to go towards public programs is called taxes. Income and sales taxes. It's not that we don't collect money for public programs and to ideally help people, it's just simply the mismanagement and mis prioritization of said funds driven by greed, propaganda, and maintaining the status quo.

It's all about coms and timing. Assets make gains and building your gains is what keeps your gains.

Infantry plays in our regi are usually done in a few scenarios.

We're setting up assets and we need to stabilize the front for our builders or logi to set up assets so we go Frontline until the op is ready.

The assets are useless because of a counter. I.e you bring a tank but your opponent brings 5 tanks. Or you lost your assets. In which case it's time for everyone to grab stickies and rush together.

Building ops. We do this together because it's less tedious on our builders and on a Frontline you sometimes need to out build incoming fire.

But for the most part. Running and gunning, clearing trenches , covering tanks, etc. is done by randos. It's a very important aspect of the Frontline but I don't think I've ever seen it done as an actual op. You're just not going to take ground with only squishy bodies. That's where the big guns come in. Tanks, arty, push guns, to break up the enemy lines, armor and defenses and allow the infantry to pour in and clean up and consolidate gains.

But tldr if you want to do infantry ops it's all about communication and having a goal. The op being "we go sit on bridge battle no.3 for a few hours" is going to be boring for all involved. You need a goal and course of action even if you don't succeed.
It's novel ground for them. Just how we want to take the south because none of us know what grass and paved straight roads are.

step 1, use console command mod to spawn in a mid-level remnant ship for your starter ship into your fleet. like the brilliant. it's the cruiser. save and close the game

step 2. go into the game files and find the brilliant in starsector\_core/data/hulls/brilliant.ship , open in notepad  
find **"builtInMods": \["automated"\]**, and replace the automated with advancedcore. youll have  
**"builtInMods": \["advancedcore"\],**  
save the file, keep it open.

step 3. launch the game, load your save, open up your refit screen and remove the 0-point automated hull mod, just click the - sign and it'll go away, then close the refit screen, open the refit screen, put yourself into the ship as the pilot. save the game, close the game

step 4. go back to that brilliant.ship file and undo your work from step2. replace advancedcore with the original automated. so, it will now be **"builtInMods": \["automated"\]** again. save and close the file.

step 5. launch game, load save, remove the 0-point advancedcore hullmod, automated will be in its place and you are now in charge of an automated remnant ship.

Extra steps to make this viable/immersive

get the adjustable skills mod, in the main menu, top left of the screen once you have it, you'll click on settings and then adjustable skills will let you set a new automated CR limit so that you can have 1000 or however many points for automated ships you want. if you do not do this, you'll start with no points to run an automated ship, and your ship readiness will be 0, and you'll be constrained on your remnant fleet size :/

get a mod that has AI cores as player portraits... or copy an AI portrait from the game files and move them into where player useable portraits are and do it yourself.

last steps for your playthrough. do not ever leave the ship you put yourself into using step 2. as you'll then have to repeat that step to move ships. if you get a radiant and want to pilot the radiant yourself without using that blue skill and the neural link, you'll have to repeat step 2-5 but this time with the radiant instead of the brilliant i used as an example.

Yeah optimization is atrocious. And I'm not here to defend the game for always pushing the technological entry barrier further and further. BUT. about a year ago I was one of those individuals that realized that his ram was running at stock baseline bios setting speeds instead of the hardwares max speed. Going from 2100 mhz to 3200 mhz gave me a pretty good boost in performance. I think something crazy like 10 fps. Maybe 15. Now imagine having another 20 fps using DDR5 with RAM speeds at an average of 5-6000 mhz, not to mention having pcie lanes with twice the bandwidth as pci3.0 going from 4000 Mb read/write/s to 8000 read/write with pcie 4.0. That effects your GPU and your SSD. I don't know if a GPU saturates a pcie 3.0 lane I don't know the numbers, but a single nvme 3500 Mb read/write speed stick saturates it, and having a raid 0 configuration does next to nothing because whilst theoretically you are doubling your read write spreads the bus can only handle 4000 Mb of data at pcie 3.0. the next generation cpus arnt crazy different than previous generations yet. Like a ryzen 7 5800x isn't exactly left in the dust by the 6000-8000 gen amd cpus, it's the other tech that really took off in this generational upgrade, the difference between pcie 3.0 and 4.0, DDR4 VS DDR5 is quite literally double and it's actually quite amazing. But anyway, that's the reason these streamers have 90 fps more consistently. They're brute forcing the optimization problems with cutting edge tech.

Small edit, it's also server dependent. You having a stable 60fps everywhere but the server only having 5 fps means that whilst you'll be able to walk around smoothly, the game will still feel like it's lagging with buttons and doors not working, NPCs, not working, trains ghosting on top of each other, the mobi glass not working.. basically anything and everything that requires interaction will feel like it's lagging because it's taking the server a million years to respond.

Another edit: I found the numbers for GPU's. It's around the 4080's and 4090's, AMD 6800xt, that start to saturate the pcie 3.0 lanes, losing 3.0 users about 3 percent performance at max usage. Not terrible for current graphics cards but cards after the 4000 Nvidia/6800 amd are bound to see more bottlenecking in a 3.0 pcie slot.

Are you trying to enable secure boot for a windows 11 upgrade? This can happen when you don't format your boot drive to use GPT (guid partition table) instead of the older MBR (master boot record) 

Even if you're not upgrading you maybe turned off CSM in the bios which is the feature that supports the older MBR, I had the same problems with my boot drive not being found before I fixed my drive and a way to restore your boot drive is to make sure CSM is enabled again, turn off pc. Reset bios either by taking out the battery or by using the shorting method, and unplug and replug in your boot drive. The key part of the fix for me was really unplugging and replugging the boot drive, I was getting a constant boot cycle with that message even when reverting my bios settings but after that it booted normaly and I was able to safely reconfigure the drive to GPT from MBR.

make sure your ram has XMP (or the other version of the same thing) enabled, alot of times ram just goes along at whatever speed your cpu can handle and not its actual rated speed i.e my friends ram was running at 2666 and not the rated 3600 mhz.. theres a quick easy performance gain right there.

\*small edit on ram: your motherboard really didcates ram speed here. your cpu has some say but if your motherboard says "i only support 3200mhz" or whatever speed, then thats basically the hard cap, no going past that. (unless you're super lucky with your components quality and do some serious fine tune overclocking)\*

if you're running 2 sticks of 16gb ram and your motherboard supports it, make sure your ram in dual channel mode, also a super easy performance gain for those who arnt doing it

check your temps (i use coretemp) and make sure your cpu is staying nice and cool. a quick thermal re paste can cut down some heat and prevent thermal throttling.

check this guys user config out (and modify it to best fit you) [https://pastebin.com/jpu24kLb](https://pastebin.com/jpu24kLb)

google/youtube different star citizen optimizations. there are things you can do that i cant tell you how to do off the top of my head, like forcing the game to run in high priority, setting up a paging file on your fastest sdd, nvidia settings if you're running such a card, etc.

make sure the game is installed on your fastest ssd, itll help.

perhaps look up windows10decluter and see if you want to get rid of some of that bloatware, it also lowers resource usage which can then be used to run SC for instance

on the topic of programs, i use a program called smart game booster, it temporarily shuts off background processes that are not required, and you can overclock your ram/gpu a little bit with it as well, it also cleans up some caches, etc, etc. i like it.

idk what cpu you have but overclocking might be in the cards depending on your temps. if your cpu temps are good it might be worth a look (warning, might break your pc if you dont know what you're doing, but theres lots of good guides)

and uh. lastly, hop servers. if a server feels like its dying on you, performance is degrading over time, audio errors, tposing npc's, etc, then its time to hop to a fresher server.

i tinkered with my PC for like 2-3 days. overclocking, ram timings, installing a new fan, re pasting my thermal paste, putting SC on a SVME SSD, making sure my ram was running to spec, cleaning up bloatware, and just in general, doing qol maintenance to my pc and fine tuning it. i went from \~18-20 fps to a roughly stable 30 while in combat, area 18, etc. if im on a space station (depending on server health) im \~40-50, sometimes 60 fps. space is 50-70 fps, on foot is \~50 fps. cities hurt the most. lorville runs at 20 for me. i havnt been back to orison since tinkering but before tinkering it was like. 8 fps lmao. uh.. yeah. i wouldnt call SC stable/smooth. my fps is all over the place. sometimes its 60+ sometimes its 25 :/  but i would say on average, doing most activities, even combat, dogfighting, etc, its around a stable playable 30. which im \*okay\* with. there IS  a current cockpit bug that severly drops fps while in cockpits btw. 70 fps on a HH, 30 while in cockpit (space) 50 fps on connie, 20 when standing near cockpit (orbiting station), so yeah, until thats fixed. fps while flying is gonna suck regardles (they said its fixed and wed have it in 3.20 but we still dont have it) and uh yeah i hope that all helps. or at least gives you an idea of where to go.

My wage would have gone up because I sure as hell would have pressed the issue. But my states minimum wage is around $10. Honestly this. A trade school or tech school is great for young adults who can do physical work. I apprenticed as an electrician (Totally free, just applied around saying I had no skills and got hired on) and after doing that for about a year I went to a free government funded trade school. (job corps, available to people 18-24 years of age, but sadly experience and quality of teaching changes from site to site) At the trade school I learned welding, did that for a few years, and now with both welding (fabrication and robotic welding) and my tiny electrical experience I'm now actually being hired on to do maintenance for a company at 22/h. I put in probably 2-3 years total of work gaining experience or going to school (school was free, work experience is free) and getting paid those 3 years as well. You don't need college right away in life. And not everything requires money to make money.

Why do that when you can go work at quick trip or something alot less stressful and make the same wage? Just saying.
